text:
maria: FYI nightly eval spike on q4-llama3-7b (int8) after yesterday's microkernel reorder merge. Failure rate up ~6% on multi-turn summary prompts. report: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/2098765432

maria: here's the condensed metric: baseline = 1.2% fail, now = 7.8% fail. top failures are repetitiveness and truncated endings.

maria: stack: A100 -> nvlink, kernel rev `kmerge@b7f9a2`, runtime change: microkernel reorder + continuous-batching tweak.

nightly-bot: nightly-eval results attached (run 2098765400). Quick stats: seed variance high on quantized variants.

devon: can you paste 2 failing examples?

maria: sure, one failure (prompt id 4231):
```
User: Summarize the following policy doc in 3 bullets...
System: [model output repeats first bullet and drops last paragraph]
```

maria: we also see odd token duplication like "the the" at end of output for ~40% of fails.

zach: looks like a sampling + kv-cache ordering issue more than pure quant. dup tokens often indicate RNG reseed or cache mismatch.

eva: I ran a quick reproduce locally with `RUN_EVAL=1 SEED=42 ./tools/nightly_eval --model q4f16-llama3-7b --batch 8` and saw same truncated ends but not all dups. attaching logs.

maria: logs show this pattern right after first attention block flush: `log: kv_index_mismatch at step 12, expected 1024 got 1016`

devon: that kv_index_mismatch is new — could be from the reorder change that alters chunking. tagging @eng-runtime.

zach: can we bisect? suspect commit b7f9a2 -> try reverting just the reorder and keep batching change. if revert fixes, we know kernel reorder is culprit.

maria: I kicked off a canary run in eu-west with revert patch: `git revert b7f9a2 --no-edit` and rebuild image `redwood/inference:canary-kvfix-209876`. started at 2098765600.

ops-bot: deploy started for redwood/inference:canary-kvfix-209876 on eu-west pool (pools: dedicated-2).

eva: quick note — quantized models have tighter alignment tolerance when kernel ordering changes, so small off-by-chunk can amplify sampling biases.

devon: if revert reduces dup/truncation then we need a targeted fix: ensure KV indexing uses absolute positions (avoid reliance on kernel internal chunk offsets).

maria: canary finished: initial metrics show fail rate back to 1.4% (+/-0.3). much better.

maria: attaching diff that should fix: add `kv_base_index = global_seq_offset` in kernel entry and assert on rebuild.

zach: nice. next steps: 1) open PR with test harness reproducer (seeded prompt set), 2) run full-nightly across all quant configs, 3) backport to 1.2.x branch, 4) roll patch to prod with small canary.

devon: I'll own the PR + test. eva can you add reproducer to nightly-eval prompt set and include a seeded unit test?

eva: on it, will add 2 failing prompts and a deterministic-run CI job.

maria: thanks. leaving this thread open until backport and rollout complete. :thumbsup:

zach: note for postmortem: add a short section on quant sensitivity to kernel ordering and a checklist item for any future microkernel reorder changes.

maria: agreed. we'll tag this under eval-regressions and kernel-reorder.
